heading: Quantum Computing Intelligence
subheading: Pure-plays, hedged giants & the road to commercial advantage
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Quantum pure-plays trade at extreme valuations (P/S ~63–509×) and are highly speculative — position sizing matters more here than anywhere else on this hub. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

tiers.label: Hedged Giants — Quantum as an Option
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Most quantum systems remain in R&D; true commercial systems are likely years away.

rows.angle: Completed its acquisition of HRL Laboratories (Aug 26), adding silicon-spin qubits, quantum sensing, materials, cryogenics, packaging and interconnect expertise to the Starling/Blue Jay roadmap (financial terms undisclosed; Boeing and GM, HRL's former owners, continue collaborating on applications). Follows last month's independently verified quantum-advantage claim (Jul 30) and the Aug 19 modular-cryostat milestone — a fast, deliberate cadence of concrete steps toward Quantum Starling (2029)
rows.watch for: Integration of HRL's silicon-spin work into the superconducting roadmap; Kookaburra qLDPC rollout; independent replication of the advantage claim; pace of the Nighthawk fleet rollout

rows.angle: Willow: below-threshold error correction confirmed as grid scaled 3×3→5×5→7×7; no incremental hardware or research catalyst in the past two weeks beyond the UK NQCC cloud-access opening and deepened NVIDIA CUDA-Q collaboration (both early-to-mid August)
rows.watch for: Gate-operation demos beyond memory preservation; output from the UK NQCC access program; any response to IBM's verified-advantage claim

rows.angle: Topological qubit program + Azure Quantum; Quantinuum/Microsoft collab reports 800× logical-vs-physical qubit fidelity on System Model H2. Quiet week for Microsoft's own program
rows.watch for: Majorana milestone reproducibility (independent critiques of the topological-qubit claim persist); Quantinuum's financials as a read-through on the partnership

rows.angle: NVQLink (built on CUDA-Q, announced Aug 17) — a universal GPU–QPU interconnect adopted by 17 quantum hardware builders and 9 national/scientific labs; no new hardware partners added in two weeks. CEO Jensen Huang continues to frame AI and quantum as complementary rather than competing
rows.watch for: NVQLink adoption at national labs; hybrid quantum-AI workloads; new builder/lab additions

private_watchlist.name: PsiQuantum
private_watchlist.note: Reportedly closed a $1.5B round (May 2026) at a ~$10.5B valuation; broke ground on its Moreton Bay Central fault-tolerant facility in Australia; expanded its DARPA agreement to $125M as one of only two firms in Stage C, the final validation stage of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. Appointed Skype co-founder and Atomico founder Niklas Zennström to its board (mid-Aug), succeeding Siraj Khaliq. Quiet week for company-specific news.

private_watchlist.name: Quantinuum
private_watchlist.note: Honeywell-backed; upsized $1.68B IPO raise at $60/share (~$12.7B valuation). Reported its first post-IPO quarter Aug 11: revenue $8M (+279% YoY) but a GAAP net loss of $597M, largely IPO-related stock comp, against $2.1B cash; FY26 revenue guidance set at $28–32M. Multi-year Oracle partnership placing its Helios trapped-ion system inside an Oracle Cloud Infrastructure AI data center, plus a $1.5M Albuquerque R&D expansion (Aug 20). Quiet week for new headlines; shares remain choppy post-IPO as the market digests burn rate against the Sol 2027 → Apollo 2029 → Lumos 2030s roadmap.

private_watchlist.name: QuEra
private_watchlist.note: $230M+ raise backed by Google Quantum AI, SoftBank, NVentures; 96 verified logical qubits — industry-leading; NVIDIA CUDA-Q/NVQLink integration partner. Outlined a gigaquop-class fault-tolerant roadmap targeting 2028–2029 (1,000+ logical qubits, 20,000+ physical qubits). No new company-specific headlines this week; note that fellow neutral-atom builder Pasqal just went public via SPAC (Aug 28) — a possible signal for QuEra's own eventual listing path.

bear_case.title: Years from commercial advantage
bear_case.description: Most systems remain R&D-phase; revenue today is mostly government contracts and research access, not commercial workloads.

bear_case.title: Valuations price in perfection — and swing hard on macro, not fundamentals
bear_case.description: The Aug 21 rebound (+7-11.5%) was fully erased by Aug 28 (IonQ -7.7%, Rigetti -5.2%, D-Wave -5.1% in a single session), driven again by rising Treasury yields (the 30-year hit a 19-year high; the 10-year sat near 4.68%) rather than company news. P/S multiples of ~63–509× still price in years of flawless execution, and that kind of round-trip on macro noise alone is a feature of the trade, not a bug.

bear_case.title: Insiders aren't buying — and leadership churn adds a new wrinkle
bear_case.description: Insiders at IonQ, Rigetti and D-Wave have collectively sold a net of roughly $863M in stock over the trailing three years, versus minimal insider buying — a persistent gap between executive selling and executive conviction. D-Wave's longtime CFO John Markovich announced his retirement Aug 25 (effective Sept 2); the company says it's unrelated to any business or reporting dispute, but the timing lands right as the bookings-to-revenue conversion story becomes the central question for the stock.

bear_case.title: Dilution as a business model
bear_case.description: Pure-plays fund R&D via repeated equity raises; share counts grow relentlessly. CHIPS Act awards to Rigetti, D-Wave and others are structured partly as government equity stakes — another layer of dilution on top. Quantinuum's own first post-IPO quarter posted a $597M GAAP net loss against $8M revenue, and newly listed Pasqal's ~100× revenue multiple on debut suggests the market is still pricing new entrants on story, not statements.

bear_case.title: Winner may not be listed
bear_case.description: IBM/Google/Microsoft or private PsiQuantum could reach fault tolerance first, stranding pure-play premiums. IBM's HRL Laboratories acquisition (Aug 26) is another reminder that the hedged giants can simply buy capability rather than build or bet on it — a structural advantage the pure-plays don't have.

catalysts.title: Pasqal debuts on Nasdaq, shares nearly double
catalysts.description: The French neutral-atom quantum builder completed its SPAC merger with Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp. II, listing under PSQL/PSQLW with ~$360M cash and a ~$2.6B pro forma valuation. Shares closed the day at $19.11, up 95.2% from the $9.79 SPAC reference price.

catalysts.title: IBM completes HRL Laboratories acquisition
catalysts.description: Adds silicon-spin qubits, quantum sensing, materials, cryogenics, and packaging/interconnect expertise to IBM's quantum hardware roadmap. Financial terms undisclosed; Boeing and GM, HRL's former owners, remain collaborators.

catalysts.title: NSF invests $290M+ in eight quantum research institutes
catalysts.description: University-led Quantum Leap Institutes at Harvard, Yale, Princeton, UC Berkeley, Chicago, Colorado, Illinois and Maryland split roughly $28-37M each over five years, covering fault tolerance, error correction, networking, sensing and simulation.

catalysts.title: D-Wave CFO John Markovich to retire Sept. 2
catalysts.description: SVP of Finance Greg Golkov, with the company since 2023 and 25+ years of finance experience, steps in as acting CFO. Stock fell roughly 8-9% on the news, erasing about $679M in market cap, though the company says the move is unrelated to any business or reporting dispute.

catalysts.title: Treasury launches Quantum-Readiness Task Force
catalysts.description: New task force will guide the financial sector's migration to post-quantum cryptography, treating the transition as core to US economic security as future quantum systems threaten to break current encryption standards.

catalysts.title: IonQ demos real-time QEC decoding on a laptop-class CPU
catalysts.description: A decoding pipeline running on a single Apple M4 Max handled MegaQuOp-scale workloads for up to 408 logical qubits and over 1 million T gates — a sign that error-correction decoding may not require exotic classical infrastructure to scale.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: IBM
positions.note: Third concrete milestone in a month: verified quantum advantage (Jul 30), modular cryostats (Aug 19), and now a completed HRL Laboratories acquisition (Aug 26) adding silicon-spin qubits and sensing capability. Nudged up a notch on the pace of execution; quantum remains a rounding error on a profitable, dividend-paying business.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: Second straight quiet week for Willow-specific news; the below-threshold error-correction claim stands unchallenged but unadvanced. Also your largest AI-sleeve holding — size the sector weight with that overlap in mind, don't double-count.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: Quiet week for Microsoft's own quantum program; the clearest read-through remains Quantinuum's Aug 11 print ($8M revenue, $597M GAAP loss). Microsoft's own exposure is immaterial to its financials either way. Also held in the AI sleeve — avoid double-counting.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: No new NVQLink hardware partners in two weeks; trimmed slightly to fund the IBM increase given the quiet stretch. Also your largest cross-sector AI holding — size for that concentration, not just the quantum optionality.

positions.name: IonQ
positions.note: Fundamentals kept improving this week (two credible new board members, a real QEC-decoding demo on commodity hardware) even as the stock round-tripped the Aug 21 rebound and got cheaper in relative terms (P/S fell to ~63x, now the lowest of the pure-play trio). Held steady rather than chased the dip.

positions.name: Rigetti
positions.note: No fresh operating news this week; stock fell in line with the sector-wide reversal. TTM revenue still $13.4M against a $5.2B market cap (P/S ~390x). Held at minimum size, no new catalyst to justify more.

positions.name: D-Wave
positions.note: The Aug 25 CFO retirement is a genuine incremental risk — it lands right as converting the 1,120% bookings surge into recognized revenue becomes the whole thesis, and a new acting CFO now owns that transition. Held at minimum size rather than trimmed further, since the company frames it as routine succession, not a red flag.

positions.name: Quantinuum
positions.note: Quiet week for new headlines. FY26 guidance of $28-32M revenue against a $12.7B IPO valuation remains the open question keeping this in Watch, not Core.

positions.name: Pasqal
positions.note: New to the list after its Aug 28 Nasdaq debut via SPAC merger, where shares nearly doubled to $19.11 on a reported ~100x revenue multiple with no independent public financials yet. Straight to Watch, not Spec, until there's at least one reporting quarter to evaluate.
